financials_interim.notes: COMPANY (standalone) basis. Same period as GROUP row -- see GROUP row's notes for shared context (share capital history, borrowings convention, subsequent event). operating_profit=(74,233) = Gross Profit (560,028) + Other Income (27,262) - Distribution Expenses (428,911) - Administration Expenses (232,612); adding Net Finance Costs (181,028) gives PBT of (255,261), ties exactly to the printed figure (no JV/ Associate lines at Company level). tax_expense=(54,642) -- printed as a positive 54,642 in the filing (un-bracketed, i.e. a tax REVERSAL/benefit, not an expense, this period), so stored as negative per the pbt-tax=pat sign convention: PBT (255,261) - tax (54,642) = (200,619), ties exactly to reported PAT. This swing from Company PBT of 22,778 (profit) in Q1 FY2025/26 to a loss of (255,261) this quarter was driven primarily by Other Income falling 82% YoY to 27,262 from 148,083 (a swing of -120,821, the single largest line-item driver, larger than the entire Gross Profit improvement of +99,611), compounded by Distribution Expenses +41% to 428,911 (+124,722) and Net Finance Costs +64% to 181,028 (+70,807) -- all growing while Gross Profit grew only 22% to 560,028. eps_basic=(1.78), only one EPS line given, eps_diluted mirrors it. short_term_borrowings=4,411,425 = current Interest Bearing Borrowings (4,071,881) PLUS Bank Overdraft (339,544); long_term_borrowings=1,783,903 (non-current Interest Bearing Borrowings). Identity check: total_liabilities (9,602,913) + total_equity (4,166,943) = 13,769,856 = total_assets, ties exactly.

Lankem Ceylon PLC (LCEY), diversified conglomerate (Capital Goods) with three operating segments -- Consumer, Industrial, Leisure -- FYE 31 March. GROUP basis. Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) vs Q1 FY2025/26 (quarter ended 30 June 2025) comparative, both explicitly presented on the face P&L (page 2). operating_profit=452,398 is the SUM of Segment Results 'Operating Profit' column (Note, page 6: Consumer 150,409 + Industrial 470,260 + Leisure (165,880) + Others (2,391) = 452,398), which reconciles to PBT via Net Finance Cost (479,332) PLUS Share of Profit/(Loss) from Joint Venture (4,572) and Associates (16,948) -- i.e. 452,398 - 479,332 - 16,948 + 4,572 = (39,310), ties exactly to reported PBT. This 452,398 figure is NOT a face-P&L subtotal (the face P&L goes straight from Gross Profit + Other Income - Distribution - Admin +/- JV/Associate - Net Finance Cost = PBT, with no 'operating profit' line), it is derived from the segment note to give a like-for-like operating profit figure. profit_before_tax=(39,310), tax_expense=105,072 (the P&L shows 'Tax (Reversal)/Expense (105,072)' in brackets = an EXPENSE of 105,072, not a reversal, for this period), profit_after_tax=(144,382): PBT (39,310) - tax (105,072) = (144,382), ties exactly. eps_basic= (0.99), only one EPS line ('Basic Earnings/(Loss) per Share'), eps_diluted mirrors it. CAUTION: eps_basic (0.99) does not tie cleanly to Loss Attributable to Owners (111,129) / shares in issue at period-end (137,255,352 per Note 7) -- that division gives 0.81, not 0.99; implied weighted-average shares from the printed EPS would be approx. 112.25mn, which does not match either the pre-rights/pre-split share count (51,470,757 at 30.06.2025) or the current 137,255,352 -- likely reflects a weighted-average-shares calculation methodology not disclosed in this interim filing (the Company completed a rights issue of 17,156,919 shares in Oct 2025 at Rs.70/share, followed by a 1-for-2 share subdivision in Dec 2025, per Note 7) -- printed EPS taken as-is, flagged as an unreconciled inconsistency rather than corrected. shares_in_issue=137,255,352 (voting shares per Note 7). short_term_borrowings=12,067,433 = current Interest Bearing Borrowings (10,586,228) PLUS Bank Overdraft (1,481,205); long_term_borrowings=4,756,874 (non-current Interest Bearing Borrowings). trade_receivables=9,257,983 ('Trade and Other Receivables', excludes separate 'Amounts Due from Related Parties -- Trade/Non-Trade' lines). trade_payables=6,060,952 ('Trade and Other Payables', excludes 'Amounts Due to Related Parties' lines). cash_and_equivalents=944,169 ('Bank & Cash Balances'; net of overdraft the cash flow statement shows (537,036), but the balance-sheet gross cash figure is used here per convention). cash_from_operations=(739,895); capex=281,552 ('Purchase & Construction of Property, Plant & Equipment'); cash_from_investing=(261,556); cash_from_financing=579,467. SEGMENTAL NOTE (page 6): Consumer segment PBT +126% YoY to 109,349 (2025: 48,386); Industrial segment PBT swung to a PROFIT of 83,061 from a LOSS of (169,424) a year earlier, driven by Industrial operating profit +232% YoY to 470,260 (2025: 141,562); Leisure segment PBT LOSS widened 375% to (232,383) from (48,887), as Leisure operating loss widened from (22,542) to (165,880) (Leisure segment revenue fell 28% YoY to 344,605 from 478,492) and Leisure's allocated net finance cost rose 152% to (66,503) from (26,345). Consolidated segment revenue: Consumer +7.9% to 2,527,263 (2,341,827), Industrial +0.6% to 6,750,352 (6,709,040), Leisure -28.0% to 344,605 (478,492), after inter-segment eliminations of (381,862) vs (217,358). Note 4 (page 7): subsequent to quarter-end, on 24 July 2026 subsidiary ACME Printing & Packaging PLC completed sale of its land and factory to Singer Sri Lanka PLC for Rs.630mn -- a non-adjusting subsequent event, not reflected in these figures. Identity check: total_liabilities (27,627,969) + total_equity (11,242,480) = 38,870,449 = total_assets, ties exactly.

interim_updates.note_text: Lankem Ceylon PLC (LCEY) narrowed its Group loss before tax by 77% YoY to Rs.39.31mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), from a loss of Rs.171.38mn in Q1 FY2025/26, on Group Revenue roughly flat at Rs.9,240.36mn (2025: Rs.9,312.00mn, -1%). Group loss for the period narrowed 35% to Rs.144.38mn (2025: Rs.222.61mn). By segment (page 6): the turnaround was driven by the Industrial segment, whose operating profit surged 232% YoY to Rs.470.26mn (2025: Rs.141.56mn), flipping Industrial's segment profit before tax to a positive Rs.83.06mn from a loss of Rs.169.42mn a year earlier -- the single largest swing in the result. Consumer segment profit before tax also improved 126% to Rs.109.35mn (2025: Rs.48.39mn) on segment revenue growth of 7.9% to Rs.2,527.26mn. Working against the improvement, the Leisure segment's loss before tax widened 375% to Rs.232.38mn (2025: Rs.48.89mn), as Leisure segment revenue fell 28.0% YoY to Rs.344.61mn (2025: Rs.478.49mn), its operating loss widened from Rs.22.54mn to Rs.165.88mn, and its allocated net finance cost rose 152% to Rs.66.50mn (2025: Rs.26.35mn) -- Leisure was the single biggest drag on the quarter. Group gross profit rose 27% to Rs.2,490.45mn (2025: Rs.1,966.29mn, gross margin 27.0% vs 21.1%) even as Group revenue was flat, implying a materially improved cost-of-sales ratio, but Distribution Expenses rose 29% to Rs.963.43mn and Administration Expenses rose 10% to Rs.1,174.23mn, while Net Finance Costs rose 28% to Rs.479.33mn (2025: Rs.373.98mn) on higher short-term and long-term interest-bearing borrowings (Group short-term borrowings, including overdraft, Rs.12,067.43mn at 30 June 2026). Tax expense more than doubled to Rs.105.07mn (2025: Rs.51.23mn), a drag that meant the PAT-loss narrowed by less (35%) than the PBT-loss narrowed (77%). At Company (standalone) level the result moved the other way: Company swung from a profit before tax of Rs.22.78mn in Q1 FY2025/26 to a loss before tax of Rs.255.26mn this quarter (-1,221%), and Company loss for the period was Rs.200.62mn versus a profit of Rs.66.59mn a year earlier (-401%) -- driven primarily by Other Income falling 82% YoY to Rs.27.26mn from Rs.148.08mn (a swing of Rs.-120.82mn, larger in absolute terms than the entire Rs.99.61mn improvement in Company gross profit), compounded by Distribution Expenses +41% to Rs.428.91mn and Net Finance Costs +64% to Rs.181.03mn. Subsequent to the quarter-end, on 24 July 2026, subsidiary ACME Printing & Packaging PLC completed the sale of its land and factory to Singer Sri Lanka PLC for Rs.630mn -- a non-adjusting event not reflected in these figures but a meaningful future capital-recycling item for the Group.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to 30 June 2026 has been collected for LCEY -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. eps_basic (Group, -0.99) does not tie cleanly to Loss Attributable to Owners (Rs.111.13mn) divided by the period-end share count of 137,255,352 (which gives -0.81) -- flagged in the GROUP row's notes as an unreconciled filing inconsistency, likely related to the Company's Oct 2025 rights issue and Dec 2025 1-for-2 share subdivision, but the exact weighted-average-share methodology is not disclosed in this interim filing. Segment-level assets/liabilities are NOT disclosed in this filing (only segment revenue, operating profit, net finance cost and PBT), so no segment balance-sheet attribution is possible. Cost-of-sales, distribution and administration expenses are not broken down by segment (only the net PBT/operating-profit roll-up is given), so the precise driver of Industrial's gross margin improvement cannot be isolated further.
interim_updates.takeaway: LCEY's Group loss before tax narrowed 77% YoY to Rs.39.31mn, but the improvement was driven almost entirely by the Industrial segment (operating profit +232% to Rs.470.26mn, PBT swinging from a Rs.169.42mn loss to an Rs.83.06mn profit), while the Leisure segment moved sharply the other way (PBT loss widening 375% to Rs.232.38mn on a 28% revenue decline) -- a genuine offsetting trend within the conglomerate rather than a uniform recovery. At Company (standalone) level the picture is worse, not better: a one-off collapse in Other Income (-82% YoY, -Rs.120.82mn) flipped the parent from profit to a Rs.255.26mn loss, a reminder that Group-level segmental improvement has not yet flowed through to the holding company's own results this quarter.

operational_highlights: Group Revenue Rs.9,240.36mn, -1% YoY (2025: Rs.9,312.00mn); Group loss before tax narrowed 77% YoY to Rs.39.31mn (2025: loss of Rs.171.38mn); Group loss for the period narrowed 35% YoY to Rs.144.38mn (2025: loss of Rs.222.61mn).

Industrial segment operating profit +232% YoY to Rs.470.26mn (2025: Rs.141.56mn), flipping Industrial segment PBT to a profit of Rs.83.06mn from a loss of Rs.169.42mn a year earlier -- the single largest driver of the Group's improved result.

Leisure segment loss before tax widened 375% YoY to Rs.232.38mn (2025: Rs.48.89mn) on a 28.0% revenue decline to Rs.344.61mn (2025: Rs.478.49mn) and a widened operating loss (Rs.165.88mn vs Rs.22.54mn) -- the single largest drag on the Group's result.
Consumer segment PBT +126% YoY to Rs.109.35mn (2025: Rs.48.39mn) on segment revenue +7.9% to Rs.2,527.26mn.
Group gross margin improved to 27.0% from 21.1% YoY even as revenue was flat, but Net Finance Costs rose 28% YoY to Rs.479.33mn and tax expense more than doubled to Rs.105.07mn (2025: Rs.51.23mn).
Company (standalone) swung from a PBT of Rs.22.78mn to a PBT loss of Rs.255.26mn (-1,221% YoY), driven primarily by Other Income falling 82% YoY to Rs.27.26mn from Rs.148.08mn.
Subsequent to quarter-end (24 July 2026, non-adjusting event), subsidiary ACME Printing & Packaging PLC completed the sale of its land and factory to Singer Sri Lanka PLC for Rs.630mn.
key_drivers: Industrial segment operating profit +232% YoY to Rs.470.26mn (2025: Rs.141.56mn) turned the segment's PBT from a Rs.169.42mn loss to an Rs.83.06mn profit -- the single largest positive swing in the Group result.

Leisure segment loss before tax widened 375% YoY to Rs.232.38mn (2025: Rs.48.89mn), on a 28.0% revenue decline to Rs.344.61mn and a widened operating loss (Rs.165.88mn vs Rs.22.54mn) plus a 152% rise in allocated net finance cost to Rs.66.50mn -- the single largest negative swing, partly offsetting the Industrial improvement.
Company (standalone) Other Income fell 82% YoY to Rs.27.26mn from Rs.148.08mn, a swing of Rs.-120.82mn that was the primary reason Company PBT flipped from a Rs.22.78mn profit to a Rs.255.26mn loss.
